prop:a-8-partition-function-identity:
Proposition Habiro coefficient a_8(X) partition-function identity: a_8(X) = \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n}. Let a_8 \in \mathbb{Z}[X] denote the top-shared (m = 8) integer Habiro coefficient of the proton and neutron in the canonical Habiro-witness convention:

  a_8(X) \;=\; X^4 + 2\,X^3 + 3\,X^2 + 5\,X + 7.

Then a_8 admits the closed form

  a_8(X) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n},

where p(n) denotes the integer partition function (Hardy–Ramanujan, OEIS A000041): p(1) = 1,\; p(2) = 2,\; p(3) = 3,\; p(4) = 5,\; p(5) = 7.

Categorical interpretation

The integer partition function p(n) appears throughout Habiro-ring / Hecke representation theory:

  • Number of Young diagrams of weight n (equivalently: partitions of n).
  • Generating function \sum_{n \geq 0} p(n)\,q^n = \prod_{k \geq 1} (1 - q^k)^{-1} = 1 / (q;q)_\infty — the Euler / Habiro generating series.
  • Dimensions of basis elements indexed by Young diagrams via the Robinson–Schensted correspondence (combined with \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim(\lambda)^2 = n!).

The appearance of p(1), p(2), p(3), p(4), p(5) as successive coefficients of a_8(X) strongly suggests that the m = 8 shell of the Habiro tower is counting partitions of n = 1, \dots, 5 — i.e., a_8(X) is the dimension-generating function of partitions fitting within the m = 8 shell.

Convention stability

This identification was made in the Habiro-witness convention (include_inter=True). The partition-function structure is much more convention-robust than the cyclotomic prefactors: it is a property of the combinatorial counting at the m = 8 shell, not of the algebraic-expansion shape, so this finding is expected to survive a change of convention.

The Hardy–Ramanujan values (1, 2, 3, 5, 7) are standard (OEIS A000041 Table 1; Andrews, The Theory of Partitions, §1.1).

Cross-references

  • Related identity: cyclotomic strand-doubling
  • categorical source: the canonical formalism

The coincidence recorded here is a categorical Habiro-shell observation rather than a new deductive argument.

prop:zeta8-witness-level2-su2:
Proposition Level-2 SU(2) Verlinde witness at q = \zeta_8: (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7 = 8, \mathrm{ord}(\sigma_i) = 8, [4]_q = 0, and the Wenzl annihilator. Let \zeta be a primitive 8th root of unity in a field R,

Proof Proof of zeta8 witness level2 su2. (1) From the cyclotomic factorisation X^8 - 1 \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{7}\,(X - \zeta_8^k), dividing by (X - 1) gives X^7 + X^6 + \cdots + 1 \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{7}\,(X - \zeta_8^k). Evaluating at X = 1: LHS = 8 and RHS = \prod_{k=1}^{7}\,(1 - \zeta_8^k) = (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7, so (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7 = 8. ∎

(2) Since \zeta_8 = e^{2\pi i / 8} is a primitive 8th root of unity, \zeta_8^k = 1 iff 8 \mid k, so \zeta_8^k \neq 1 for 1 \leq k \leq 7. The Hecke quadratic relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 at q = \zeta_8 gives eigenvalues \sigma_i \in \{\zeta_8, -\zeta_8^{-1}\}. Both eigenvalues have order 8: \zeta_8 directly, and -\zeta_8^{-1} = \zeta_8^4 \cdot \zeta_8^{-1} = \zeta_8^3 which is also a primitive 8th root of unity. The order of \sigma_i is therefore \mathrm{lcm}(8, 8) = 8. ∎

(3) At q = \zeta_8, q^4 = (e^{i\pi/4})^4 = e^{i\pi} = -1, so q^4 = -1 = q^{-4}, giving q^4 - q^{-4} = 0. Since q - q^{-1} \neq 0 (as \zeta_8 \neq \pm 1), [4]_q = 0/(q - q^{-1}) = 0. ∎

prop:confined-knot-binding:
Proposition Confined knot binding mechanism: character ratio decomposition per jet level. Let \beta \in H_3(R, q) be a confined nuclear braid built from crossing operators at generators \sigma_{i_k}. The Wedderburn-Artin decomposition separates each crossing's contribution into three channels:

  \hat{V}(c, d)
  = W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{sym}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{std}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{alt}}(c, d).

The extremal contributions exactly cancel for symmetric crossings encoding the proton-neutron force. The binding volume transfers entirely to the standard representation:

  \hat{V}_{\mathrm{pn}}
  = W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \Bigl(z - \frac{h_{\mathrm{A}}}{2}\Bigr).

The 2-dimensional standard representation creates non-commuting cross-channel interactions between adjacent generators. This generates the Markov-weighted pair interaction term \delta_{\times}.

For an A-nucleon system constructed sequentially through quark, nucleon, and nuclear jet levels, the character ratio measures the volume departure from the free constituents. The total knot factor multiplies these strict, empirically-independent character ratios across all levels.

The three levels are not in one convention

The product "across all levels" needs the three character ratios to be ratios of the same functional. They are not. The quark and nucleon levels are Markov traces — weights y_\lambda at z = q^3/(q^2+1) (Wenzl level r = 2), which admits only \le 2-row shapes. The nuclear-jet level uses the conjectural classical-limit jet weight \tilde w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[n]_q! summed over all partitions, and those two weight systems form distinct families on every stratum. On H_3:

(2,1) 0.247297886748035 0.660673773661173

\sum_\lambda \dim(\lambda)\,y_\lambda = 1 exactly, as a normalised trace must; \sum_\lambda \tilde w_\lambda = 0.98744 at q_0. The (1,1,1) row is structural — z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 point of the Ocneanu family, so y_\lambda = 0 once \lambda has more than two rows, while \tilde w is a ratio of positive quantum integers. The jet measure charges a block the Markov trace annihilates.

The two disagree about the pn bond in particular, and not by a rescale: the single interface letter traces to z + d_{pn} = 0.508229789376739 under y, and to 0.000071511999729 under \tilde w — a factor of 7107, because \tilde w weights the two blocks equally and d_{pn} is their midpoint up to \delta, making pn its near-null vector.

prop:canonical-closure-torus-chain:
Proposition The canonical closure is a chain of (2,\mathrm{odd})-torus knots: bridge number 2A+1 and total curvature 2\pi(2A+1). Resolve each averaged letter of the canonical word of the atomic braid to a crossing sign (either branch) and freely reduce. The result is a chain form

  W_A \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{A-1} \sigma_{3k}^{\,a_k}\,\sigma_{3k+1}^{\,b_k}\,\sigma_{3k+2}^{\,\varepsilon_k}
  \qquad(\text{no } \varepsilon \text{ on the last block}),

each generator appearing exactly once, in order, as a single power, with a_k odd, b_k even and non-zero, and \varepsilon_k = \pm 1. Consequently its closure is the linear connected sum of the torus links T(2, e_i) along shared strands: A knots T(2, a_k) and one unknot, consecutive components linked with \mathrm{lk} = b_k/2; the A-1 interface generators are connected-sum bands with the unknot and drop out, leaving the (2A+1)-strand chain W'_A = \prod_k \sigma_{2k}^{a_k}\sigma_{2k+1}^{b_k} with the same closure. Hence

  \mu = A+1,\qquad \#\{\text{knotted components}\} = A,\qquad b(L) = 2A+1,
  \qquad \inf_{\text{isotopy class}} \int \kappa\, ds \;=\; 2\pi\,(2A+1).

The exponents

Read off the canonical interface composition block by block (verified for every isotope through A = 12 on both branches):

a_k (generator 3k) b_k (generator 3k+1) \varepsilon_k (interface 3k+2)
averaged \to \sigma 7 for every nucleon -2 (proton), -4 (neutron) +1 (pp), -1 (nn), +1 (pn)
averaged \to \sigma^{-1} 5 (proton), 3 (neutron) -4 for every nucleon +1 (pp), -1 (nn), -1 (pn)

So on the \sigma branch every knotted component is T(2,7); on the \sigma^{-1} branch protons give T(2,5) and neutrons T(2,3). The linking graph is the path with \mathrm{lk}(k, k+1) = b_k/2 \in \{-1, -2\}, the sublinks of consecutive pairs are not (2, 2\,\mathrm{lk})-torus links, and the components are not unknots -- which is a second, independent reason the Borromean (Brunnian) picture does not describe this closure.

Proof

Chain form. Each nucleon block uses generator 3k seven times and generator 3k+1 four times, in that order, and the interface to the next block is the single generator 3k+2; resolving and freely reducing gives the table.

Connected sum. A closed braid whose word is a product of sub-words on strand sets overlapping in exactly one strand is the connected sum of the closures of the sub-words along that strand [birman1974]; iterating gives the linear chain of T(2, e_i). Since T(2, \pm 1) is the unknot and a connected sum with the unknot is the identity, each \sigma_{3k+2}^{\pm 1} can be deleted and the indices closed up: W'_A has the same closure.

Bridge number. A closed n-braid is an n-bridge presentation, so b(L) \le 2A+1. Each T(2, a_k) with a_k \ge 3 odd has bridge number 2 and the unknot has 1; bridge number is at least the sum over components, so b(L) \ge 2A + 1.

Curvature. Milnor [milnor1950]: the infimum of total curvature over an isotopy class equals 2\pi times the bridge number. (Under Crofton, total curvature is \pi times the average number of critical points of the height functions -- the oscillation count, integrated -- which is where the serpenoid picture that prompted this result becomes exact.)

What is proved, what is checked, what is cited

The algebra is proved: the Seifert form of T(2,n) is unimodular for every odd n; the continuant of V - X V^{\mathsf T} satisfies (X+1) D_{2g} = X^{2g+1} + 1, so the Alexander polynomial is (X^n+1)/(X+1) and divides X^{2n}-1; the floor 2A+1 \le b \le 3A is bookkeeping from \mu = A+1 and A knotted components. The chain form and its exponents are verified exactly for A \le 12, and the symbolic predictions -- components, knot types, linking, and that W'_A closes to the same link (Jones polynomial and per-component Jones) -- for A \le 4, by symbolic computation; a computational instance at A \le 6 is obtained via Reidemeister simplification and Vogel's algorithm. The two topological facts above and Milnor's theorem are cited, not proved here, and the identification of the components from their Jones polynomials is computational.

Scope

Everything here is per classical branch: the canonical Hecke element is not a link, its 2A+1 averaged letters have no crossing sign, and a statement about the un-resolved object does not exist. Nothing here connects curvature to binding, and nothing supplies the twist: the osculating circle sees \kappa and is blind to \tau, and the framing datum the binding gap needs lives in the torsion.

Proposition Deformed exchange criticality: g^2\,(1+[2]_v^2)=1 characterizes the pn-bond magnitude, with 5+(v-v^{-1})^2 = 1+[2]_v^2. Let R be a commutative ring, v \in R invertible, [2]_v = v + v^{-1}, and let

\begin{align*}
  M(b) &= \begin{pmatrix} 1 & b \\ b & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  &S(a,w) &= \begin{pmatrix}
     0 & a & w & w\\
     a & 0 & w & w\\
     w & w & 0 & -a\\
     w & w & -a & 0
  \end{pmatrix}
\end{align*}

denote the symmetric-sector exchange matrix and the uniform-magnitude [1^4] complete-graph exchange matrix on nucleon blocks [p,p,n,n]. Then:

  1. (Deformation identity) 5 + (v - v^{-1})^2 = 1 + [2]_v^2.
  2. (Cayley–Hamilton form) M(b)^2 = (1 + b^2)\cdot\mathbf{1}; in particular the classical b = 2 gives the scalar 5.
  3. (Marginal stability) \det\bigl(\mathbf{1} + g\,M(b)\bigr) = 1 - g^2(1+b^2) for every b; hence, specializing to the deformed pn-degree b = [2]_v, any g with g^2(1 + [2]_v^2) = 1 is exactly the point where the deformed symmetric-sector determinant \det\bigl(\mathbf{1} + g\,M([2]_v)\bigr) vanishes.
  4. (pn-sign blindness) With D = \mathrm{diag}(1,1,-1,-1) one has D\,S(a,w)\,D = S(a,-w), and consequently \det(\mathbf{1} + S(a,w)) = \det(\mathbf{1} + S(a,-w)) and \mathrm{tr}\bigl(T\,S(a,w)^k\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}\bigl(T\,S(a,-w)^k\bigr) for every k and every T commuting with D.

In particular the magnitude g with g^2(1+[2]_v^2) = 1 equals z/\sqrt{1+z^2} evaluated at the Markov bond factor z = 1/[2]_v whenever square roots are available, and satisfies g^2\,(5 + (v-v^{-1})^2) = 1 by item 1.

Scope

prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price:
Proposition Mass-formula coefficients as shadow prices of the Frobenius positivity constraints. Each coefficient of the QOU mass formula is the shadow price (LP dual variable) of the corresponding partition's Frobenius positivity constraint in a partition-indexed operator-selection program.

Note (scope of the program). The statement is about a program whose Frobenius positivity constraints are indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n — one per Wedderburn block. It is not a claim about the operator-selection LP as that block states it, which indexes its constraints by NF basis element (d = n! of them, so six against three partitions at n = 3). Two consequences follow, and neither is a claim that the coefficients are wrong:

  1. The net-constraint dual of the NF-indexed LP is identically zero. Since the NF basis contains the identity, its first Frobenius row is the objective vector, so that program minimises t \cdot x subject to t \cdot x \ge 0; its optimal value is 0 for every n_{\mathrm{target}}, and by strong duality y_0^\ast = 0. Any quantity recovered by dividing by y_0^\ast is undefined — see the degeneracy section.
  2. The per-partition Frobenius duals are a separate question and are not contradicted. At H_3 the committed partition-indexed solve gives y^\ast_{(3)} = y^\ast_{(2,1)} = 1 and y^\ast_{(1^3)} = 0, so c_\lambda = y^\ast_\lambda\, m_e is satisfiable on the nonzero blocks. The vanishing block is the \mathrm{SU}(2) specialisation, not a failure of the pairing: every \ell(\lambda) \ge 3 weight vanishes identically, which is why a partition-indexed program must be posed on the two-row quotient.

Note (closed-form shifted weight vs. LP dual). The closed-form formula often paired with this proposition evaluates y_\lambda = w_\lambda/d_\lambda - 1/[k]_q! in closed form and solves no program. Its 1/[k]_q! term is \min_\lambda (w_\lambda/d_\lambda), so it subtracts a constant that zeroes exactly the two one-dimensional blocks (k) and (1^k) at every level; it is not the dual variable of any normalisation constraint, and it is not y_0^\ast, which is 0.
prf:mass-coefficient-shadow-price:
Proof Proof of mass coefficient shadow price. The operator selection LP at Hecke level k selects the nuclear operator \Phi = \sum_i x_i b_i \in H_k(R, q) by:

  \min_x \; \sum_i t_i \, x_i
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \mathbf{1}^T x = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \;\;
  G x \geq 0

where t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) and G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) is the Frobenius Gram matrix.

In the Wedderburn basis \{e^\lambda_{ij}\}, the Gram matrix block-diagonalises: G = \bigoplus_\lambda G_\lambda with G_\lambda = (w_\lambda / d_\lambda) \, I_{d_\lambda^2}, where w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! and d_\lambda = \dim(\lambda). The Frobenius constraint Gx \geq 0 separates into one constraint per partition \lambda:

  \langle \Phi, \pi_\lambda \rangle_F
  = \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda} \, \mathrm{tr}(\Phi_\lambda)
  \geq 0

where \Phi_\lambda is the projection of \Phi onto the \lambda-block and \pi_\lambda is the central idempotent.

Dual program. The dual of the spectral LP is:

  \max_{u_0, \, u_\lambda \geq 0} \;\; n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0
  \text{s.t.} \quad
  u_0 + \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda} \, u_\lambda
  \leq \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda}
  \quad \forall \, \lambda \vdash k

By strong duality (the feasible set is non-empty and bounded), primal and dual optima coincide. The optimal dual variables u_\lambda^* satisfy complementary slackness:

  u_\lambda^* \cdot \langle \Phi^*, \pi_\lambda \rangle_F = 0

Factorisation. For the nuclear braid \Phi(Z,N), each dual variable factors as:

  u_\lambda^*(Z,N) = C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z,N,A)

where:

  1. C_\lambda is a q-integer product determined by the partition algebra (hooks, contents, Frobenius coordinates) — independent of any nuclear datum.

  2. S_\lambda(Z,N,A) is the scaling function determined by the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_\square (j-i):

    • c(\lambda) > 0: volume-type (A-dependent)
    • c(\lambda) = 0: isospin-type (T(T+1)/A^p)
    • c(\lambda) < 0: charge-type (Z-dependent)

The factorisation is unique because the Wedderburn blocks are orthogonal under the Frobenius pairing: different partitions contribute to linearly independent scaling functions.

Mass-formula decomposition. The binding energy is:

  B(Z,N) = \sum_{\lambda} C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z,N,A)
           \cdot m_e

Each term of the QOU six-term mass formula is one shadow price u_\lambda^* (or the sum of a conjugate pair u_\lambda^* + u_{\lambda'}^* when \lambda' = \lambda^\vee). The coefficient C_\lambda \cdot m_e is the shadow price evaluated at the normalisation point where S_\lambda = 1.

Corollary (coefficient at each level). By the Markov-trace normalization \sum_\lambda d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1, the per-level budget is set by the Hecke-level scale [k]_q! (the q-factorial at level k). This constrains the total shadow-price budget: the normalization is the dual feasibility constraint ensuring all u_\lambda^* are consistent. The budget at level k is [k]_q!; the marginal budget from advancing k \to k+1 is [k+1]_q! - [k]_q! = [k]_q! \cdot ([k+1]_q - 1).

Corollary (branching rule for coefficients). The branching \mathrm{Res}^{H_{k+1}}_{H_k} V_\mu = \bigoplus_{\lambda} V_\lambda induces a constraint on the level-(k{+}1) shadow prices via Frobenius reciprocity:

  C_\mu = \sum_{\lambda : \lambda \nearrow \mu}
    \frac{\dim_q(\mu)}
         {\sum_{\mu' : \lambda \nearrow \mu'} \dim_q(\mu')}
    \cdot C_\lambda

where \lambda \nearrow \mu denotes that \mu is obtained from \lambda by adding one cell. This propagates known coefficients from level k to level k{+}1 without fitting. \square
prop:unstable-atom-decay-channel:
Proposition Uniqueness of the decay channel off the boundary variety. Let K be an atom-knot that is unstable at q, and let \lambda^* be a candidate decay channel. Assume q lies off the boundary variety, and assume the LP-duality selection input of the shadow-price proposition: off the boundary variety, every partition that minimises the constraint-violation energy equals \lambda^*. Then:

  2. if the energy E(\lambda^*, \cdot) is continuous on [q_1, q_2] with E(\lambda^*, q_1) \le 0 \le E(\lambda^*, q_2), then E(\lambda^*, q^*) = 0 for some q^* \in [q_1, q_2].

prf:unstable-atom-decay-channel:
Proof Proof of unstable atom decay channel. Scope of the LP-relaxation argument. The proof below was formulated for an existential form of stability requiring some non-negative integer vector x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N to satisfy \mathrm{G}(q)\,x \geq 0 (which is trivially satisfied by x = 0). Under the universal formulation of stability applied to the fixed normal-form coefficient vector x(K, q) of T_w, the violated constraint is read directly as \arg\min_\gamma (\mathrm{G}(q)\,x(K, q))_\gamma whenever x(K, q) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N; the extension to signed normal-form coefficient vectors and its generic uniqueness remain open.

Proof. Since K is unstable, the ILP \{x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N : \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0\} has no solution within the confinement filtration J^{\ell(K, q)}(q).

Run the LP relaxation \{x \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N : \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0\}. This is always feasible. The trivial x = 0 vector satisfies G \cdot 0 = 0 \geq 0, and the relaxation is the convex hull of integer solutions. Pick the unique optimal vertex x^*_{LP} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N closest to an integer point.

The violated constraint is:

  \gamma^*(K, q)
  \;:=\;
  \arg\min_\gamma\;
    (\mathrm{G}(q)\, \lceil x^*_{LP} \rceil)_\gamma,

which is the constraint with the smallest (most negative) Frobenius positivity value at the rounded integer point. By LP duality (mass-coefficient-shadow-price), this corresponds to a unique partition \lambda^*(K, q). This is the operator e_{\lambda^*} that fails to satisfy positivity.

Uniqueness: if two distinct partitions \lambda_1, \lambda_2 both achieve the minimum at the same integer point, they have identical shadow prices at q. That is, |y_{\lambda_1}(q)| = |y_{\lambda_2}(q)|. These lie on the boundary variety (local shadow ordering) of measure zero. Generically (off the boundary variety), \lambda^* is unique. \square

Connection to phase boundary. An atom that is stable at q_1 and unstable at q_2 necessarily crosses a q^* \in [q_1, q_2] where E(\lambda^*, q^*) = |y_{\lambda^*}(q^*)| = 0. The LP boundary for the violated constraint vanishes. Crossing q^* flips ILP feasibility.
rem:unstable-atom-decay-phase:
Remark Decay channel, phase boundary, and phase-interior shortcut. Decay channel. An unstable atom must drop to a lower confinement level. It either adjoins a higher-energy operator (which then becomes available, raising \ell and enlarging the ILP search space) or transitions to a different atom-knot K' at the same or lower level. The decay product is determined by:

  1. Identifying the violated constraint \gamma^* = \arg\min_\gamma (\mathrm{G}(q) x)_\gamma over all ILP-attempted x. This is the constraint with the smallest shadow price contribution.
  2. Identifying the decay channel as the operator e_{\lambda^*} whose contribution to \gamma^* is most negative. This is the operator that fails to satisfy Frobenius positivity.
  3. Obtaining the daughter atom K' by removing e_{\lambda^*} from the normal form and re-running the ILP on the reduced primitive set.

This matches the classical \beta-decay picture. An unstable nucleus emits the operator that violates positivity, and the daughter has fewer constraints.

Phase boundary. An atom that is stable at q_1 and unstable at q_2 necessarily has a boundary point q^* \in [q_1, q_2] where the relevant shadow price vanishes:

  E(\lambda^*, q^*)
  \;=\;
  |y_{\lambda^*}(q^*)|
  \;=\;
  0.

Crossing q^* is a categorical phase transition. The operator \lambda^* disappears from the LP-dual basis, the filtration restructures, and the ILP feasibility flips. This is the operator-theoretic origin of the empirical observation that isotope stability changes abruptly between adjacent A values (e.g. {}^{12}\mathrm{C} is stable, but {}^{14}\mathrm{C} is unstable).

The per-generator \hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}} values (mass-endomorphism-tower) are locally constant in q. where w_\lambda is the q-deformed Wedderburn weight, d_\lambda = \dim V_\lambda, and \mu_\lambda = \sum_{\square \in \lambda} [c(\square)]_q\,[c(\square)+1]_q is the Jucys–Murphy q-Casimir eigenvalue on the \lambda-block, so that \varrho_\lambda is the q-resolvent evaluated at the Planck-step Reeb frequency s_\ast. The per-partition contribution is

  B_\lambda(Z, N)
  = m_e \cdot H_q(\lambda) \cdot u_\lambda \cdot \varrho_\lambda(s_\ast) \cdot
    \big( \ln\big| \mathrm{tr}\, \mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)} \big| -
          \ln d_\lambda \big),

and the total unified correction is the sum of B_\lambda(Z, N) over every enumerated \lambda.

Only multi-dimensional mixing partitions carry a non-zero u_\lambda: the subtrahend 1/[k]_q! is exactly \min_\lambda (w_\lambda / d_\lambda), so it annihilates the two one-dimensional blocks (k) and (1^k) at every level and nothing else.

The formulation bypasses special-case branching entirely. Each atomic step computes an independent energy increment from the transition trace difference, and the increments telescope, so the per-partition total depends on the running product only through its final trace. The process extracts the binding increment via identical algebraic mechanisms across all values of A.

No sign selection on blocks

The sum above is unrestricted. Restricting it to those \lambda with \mathrm{tr}\, \mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)} \le 0 is not a consequence of the Frobenius positivity constraint, as the following shows.

Complementary slackness for a Frobenius positivity constraint \langle \Phi, \pi_\lambda \rangle \ge 0 makes tight mean \mathrm{tr} = 0, not \mathrm{tr} \le 0. Under that reading every selected block contributes the same constant and the total reads nothing about the nucleus; the selected set also meets the domain of \ln|\cdot| nowhere.

The operator-selection programme is degenerate as well: its net-constraint dual vanishes identically and its minimiser set is a positive-dimensional face, so complementary slackness on that programme cannot single out a partition set at all.

Nor was the restriction a perturbation. Summing over all \lambda instead gives a total larger by a factor of 1.93 at A = 2 and 1.95 at A = 4, evaluated at the production truncation k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 11; at k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 4 the same two factors are 4.60 and 3.40. The quantity is strongly truncation-dependent — the unrestricted A = 2 total spans a factor of 43 across k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 4 \ldots 11 — so neither factor means anything quoted without its tier. The two readings coincide only when the excluded blocks happen to cancel exactly.

Removing the restriction is not an accuracy improvement. At A = 2 the AME2020 binding is +2.2246\;\mathrm{MeV}, and the restricted and unrestricted totals are both negative, the unrestricted one lying further from the measured value. What the removal discards is a selection step whose stated justification is false, not a term that was bringing the prediction closer to the data.

The name u_\lambda is a per-partition weight in closed form. It is not a shadow price of any programme — it is not the net-constraint dual, which vanishes, and at H_3 it is (0,\,0.16695,\,0) against the partition-indexed Frobenius duals (1,\,1,\,0) of the mass-coefficient block. It is written y_\lambda in the compute, where it is evaluated by hecke_core_legacy.lp_shadow_price; that name is historical and is not the Markov partition weight of the same glyph.

Proof Proof of unified iterative correction. By prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, the BW coefficient of partition \lambda is the LP-dual variable u_\lambda^* = C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z, N, A). The categorical scale C_\lambda = m_e \cdot H_q(\lambda) (the q-hook product over the Young diagram of \lambda) is the universal constant determined by the partition algebra, with no nuclear data; the scaling function S_\lambda(Z, N, A) is realised at each step as \ln|\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)}| - \ln d_\lambda via the Young seminormal representation.

For \lambda = (2,2) \vdash 4 this recovers the dedicated Wigner identity (prop:wigner-np-pairing): H_q((2,2)) = [3]_q \cdot [2]_q^2; for \lambda = (2,1) \vdash 3 it reproduces the volume / surface / Coulomb decomposition through their image under the Wedderburn embedding — a step this proof does not discharge, and which the corpus still cannot supply.

The obstruction is one of shape. The Wedderburn embedding is a concrete construction, but it has type \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda} \to M_{n!}: it assembles blocks into one matrix rather than splitting one block's scalar C_{(2,1)} into three coefficients. The landing in M_{n!} is additionally conditional on the RSK identity \sum_\lambda (f^\lambda)^2 = n!, carried as a named hypothesis and discharged by nothing here.

That objection is now a theorem, not a remark . The naive form — "three independent coefficients cannot come from one scalar" — is false, since one real encodes three set-theoretically. Under linearity, which this corpus already assumes for the Markov trace, it is true: that trace factors through the block traces, so a functional of that form supported at a single \lambda is exactly c_\lambda \cdot \operatorname{tr}(x_\lambda) — one coefficient against one number — and any three such are linearly dependent, with an explicit witness .

This does not make the clause false; it rules out the route the clause names, whenever that route is linear, factors through the Markov trace, and is localised at (2,1). It also says where the room is, which is the more useful half: f^{(2,1)} = 2, so the block is M_2(\mathbb{R}) — four real dimensions, of which the trace reads one. The information wanted is present in the block and destroyed by tracing it — itself now a theorem: whenever a block has dimension at least 2 there are distinct decompositions on which every block trace agrees, so every trace-factoring functional, the Markov trace included, takes the same value on both. Instantiating that at (2,1) needs f^{(2,1)} = 2; that value is established (via the Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length formula), so the instance at (2,1) holds unconditionally. The general theorems keep the bound as a hypothesis because they are about any block of dimension \geq 2. The boundary is real: f^{(1,1)} = 1, so at the charge shape the block is its trace and none of this applies. A derivation reading the block rather than its trace is not blocked by any of this — and that is now constructive rather than merely permitted: there exist three linearly independent block-reading functionals at (2,1), the exact complement of the three trace-factoring ones being dependent. It does not identify those three with volume, surface and Coulomb; three independent functionals existing is a necessary condition for such a match, not evidence of one. So the clause is still an open obligation, not a derivation; for higher partitions it adds the form-factor, pn-correlation, and {[3,2,1]} pn-invisible corrections.

By the Markov-trace normalization (the per-level budget is the Hecke-level scale [k]_q!, k fixed), the dual shadow prices satisfy a single budget constraint per Hecke level; by Frobenius reciprocity (prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, branching corollary), shadow prices at level k+1 are determined by those at level k. Telescoping per-step log-trace differences across k = 1, \ldots, A yields the closed-form B_\lambda.

The Kerov q-hook walk [kerov1996] gives the iterative Markov-chain interpretation of \mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..k)} as a transition kernel on the Young lattice; the Féray–Méliot q-Plancherel CLT [feray-meliot2012] guarantees the asymptotic convergence of the accumulator at rate O(1/\sqrt{A}) across Hecke levels.

The three legacy mechanisms specialise:

  • deuteron (A = 2, dedicated \alpha_{\mathrm{Borromean}} \cdot \hat V_e): the A = 2 slice of the LP-dual accumulator, dominated by the (2,1) and (2,2) shadow prices;
  • knot factor (A = 3, 4, dedicated a(N) = 1 - h^2, (1 - h^2)^2): the A = 3, 4 slices of the LP-dual accumulator, where the (2,1) and (3,1) contributions reproduce the figure-eight and Borromean amphicheiral factors;
  • Wigner energy (k = 4, dedicated -\Delta_W \cdot T(T+1)/A): the k = 4 self-conjugate shadow price \lambda = (2,2), which vanishes on isolated pn crossings (extremal cancellation, prop:confined-knot-binding) but is nonzero on collective pn patterns. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) no self-conjugate partition beyond k = 4 can contribute: self-conjugacy forces \ell(\lambda) = \lambda_1, so the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 admits only (1), (2,1) and (2,2), and a block with \tilde w_\lambda = 0 has C_\lambda = 0 and hence u_\lambda^* = 0 at every (Z, N) — the vanishing is upstream of the scaling function, so no S_\lambda restores it.

\square

Algorithm summary (one block, no special cases, A = 1 onward):

for k in 2..K_PARTITION_MAX:
  for partition λ of k:
    H_q(λ)   = ∏_{x∈λ} [h_x]_q

prop:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-du: Proposition Frobenius self-duality of (H_n(R,q),\tau) forces \tau-extraction to produce LP-dual variables. Let I_n \subset H_n(R,q) be the radical of the Markov trace \tau, the sum of the Wedderburn blocks V_\lambda with y_\lambda = 0. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) these are the shapes with three or more rows, so I_n = 0 for n \le 2 and H_n/I_n = TL_n(q). The trace descends to a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear pairing on TL_n(q). This makes (TL_n(q),\tau) a Frobenius algebra, hence canonically isomorphic to its R-linear dual. Under this isomorphism, the primal LP variable x \in TL_n and the dual LP variable u \in TL_n^* live in the same space, and the Observation Frame \mathrm{Obs}_\tau(a) := \tau(a \cdot -) extracts the shadow-price representative of every observable.
prf:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-dua:
Proof Proof of frobenius self duality forces lp dual extraction. Step 1: Frobenius pairing. The Markov trace \tau : H_n(R,q) \to R satisfies \tau(ab) = \tau(ba) for all a,b \in H_n, and \tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda by the Wedderburn trace identity. On a block with y_\lambda \neq 0 the pairing (a,b) \mapsto y_\lambda \operatorname{tr}(a_\lambda b_\lambda) is the non-degenerate matrix-trace pairing; on a block with y_\lambda = 0 it vanishes identically. So the radical of \langle a,b\rangle_\tau := \tau(ab) is I_n = \bigoplus_{y_\lambda = 0} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda). At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the weights are y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 and y_{(1^3)} = 0 at n = 3, and in general every shape with three or more rows has y_\lambda = 0; so \tau is degenerate on H_n for n \ge 3. It descends to a non-degenerate symmetric pairing on TL_n(q) = H_n/I_n, making (TL_n(q), \tau) a Frobenius algebra in the sense of Frobenius (1903) and Nakayama (1939). Steps 2–5 are carried out on TL_n(q); read H_n there as TL_n.

Step 2: Self-duality isomorphism. The map

  \Phi_\tau : H_n(R,q) \longrightarrow H_n(R,q)^*,
  \quad a \mapsto \big(b \mapsto \tau(ab)\big)

is an isomorphism of R-modules (and a bimodule isomorphism when both sides carry the regular bimodule structure). This is the canonical Frobenius self-duality.

Step 3: Operator-selection LP under self-duality. The operator-selection LP at level n has primal:

  \min_{x \in H_n} \tau(\Theta \cdot x)
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \tau(\mathbf{1} \cdot x) = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \;\;
  \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0 \;\; \forall \lambda

where \Theta is the cost operator (knot-energy weight) and \pi_\lambda is the central idempotent for block V_\lambda.

The dual program is

  \max_{u_0, u_\lambda \geq 0} n_{\mathrm{target}} u_0
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  u_0 \mathbf{1} + \sum_\lambda u_\lambda \pi_\lambda
  \;\preceq_\tau\; \Theta

where \preceq_\tau denotes the partial order induced by the Frobenius pairing: a \preceq_\tau b \iff \tau(c \cdot (b - a)) \geq 0 for all c \succeq_\tau 0.

Step 4: Primal-dual coincidence (under standard LP hypotheses). Under \Phi_\tau, the primal feasible set P = \{x \in H_n : \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0\} is \Phi_\tau-isomorphic to the dual feasible cone D = \{u : u \succeq_\tau 0\}. The cost functional x \mapsto \tau(\Theta \cdot x) is, under \Phi_\tau, identified with the dual objective u \mapsto \langle u, \Theta \rangle. Strong duality holds whenever the standard finite- dimensional LP regularity conditions are met — primal feasibility and primal boundedness (or, equivalently for the canonical operator-selection LP of Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality, existence of a strictly feasible point, i.e. Slater's condition). For the per-atom operator-selection LP these hypotheses are verified by direct construction in Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality; the proposition above adds structurally that the primal- dual identification itself does not require additional analytic argument because the Frobenius pairing is non- degenerate. Strong duality + the Frobenius identification together imply the \tau-extraction is the dual map.

Step 5: τ-extraction is the dual map. The Observation Frame \mathrm{Obs}_\tau : H_n(R,q) \to H_n(R,q)^* defined by \mathrm{Obs}_\tau(a) = \tau(a \cdot -) is \Phi_\tau. Therefore, an observable produced by τ-extraction is, by definition, a dual-space element.

Corollary. Every coefficient c_\lambda \in \mathbb{R} that arises as a τ-extracted observable from a Frobenius-positivity-constrained LP is a shadow price u_\lambda^* of the corresponding constraint. This is not a derivation; it is the structure of the observation frame in a Frobenius-self-dual category. \square

Corollary (mass-formula coefficients are LP-dual variables). By mass-coefficient-shadow-price, every QOU mass-formula coefficient C_\lambda at every Hecke level k is the τ-extraction of a shadow price; by the proposition above, this is the only form a τ-extracted observable can take in a Frobenius-self-dual category. The mass formula is therefore canonically a sum of LP-dual variables:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \sum_\ell u^{(\ell)*}

where u^{(\ell)*} is the optimal LP-dual at filtration level \ell (see mass-formula-iterative-lp-dual).
rem:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-dua: Remark Categorical content: self-duality of \mathbf{Rep}(H_n) behind the LP dual. The Frobenius self-duality holds at the categorical level: the rigid monoidal category \mathbf{Rep}(H_n(R,q)) is self-dual under the \tau-pairing, and \tau is precisely the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}_C on the unit object. The "primal vs. dual" distinction in the LP is a K-theoretic shadow of the categorical self-duality; there is no other choice.
prop:subset-cumulant-recursion:
Proposition Subset cumulants of the bond model: reconstruction, the c_k-only recursion, and vanishing across a split. Let L be a function on subsets S of the A nucleons of an atomic braid with L(\varnothing) = 0, and define its Möbius cumulants over the Boolean lattice by the recursion

  \mathrm{cum}(S) \;=\; L(S) \;-\; \sum_{T \subsetneq S} \mathrm{cum}(T).

Then, with no further hypothesis on L:

  1. (Reconstruction.) \displaystyle \sum_{T \subseteq S} \mathrm{cum}(T) = L(S) for every S.
  2. (The c_k-only recursion.) If L(S) depends only on |S|, say L(S) = f(|S|), then \mathrm{cum}(S) = c_{|S|} where 
      c_k \;=\; f(k) \;-\; \sum_{j<k} \binom{k}{j}\, c_j .
  3. (Mixed cumulants vanish across an additive split.) If the nucleons split as \mathcal{A} \sqcup \mathcal{B} and L(S) = L(S \cap \mathcal{A}) + L(S \cap \mathcal{B}) for every S, then \mathrm{cum}(S) = 0 whenever S meets both \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{B}.

What it is for

The bond model of binding reads the many-body content of a nucleus off the Markov trace: with bonds placed among the nucleons in S, in the interleaved order the canonical interface composition fixes, one sets L(S) = \log\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{free}} / \mathrm{tr}_S\bigr) and reads the genuine k-body term as the order-k cumulant. Item 1 is what makes the cumulants a decomposition of the full L rather than a rearrangement of it; item 3 is what makes them cumulants in the standard sense -- independence kills every mixed one -- and it is the property that turns the Markov trace's multiplicativity on split links (an unbonded nucleon is a separate component, contributing equally to numerator and denominator) into additivity of L on disjoint bonded parts.

Item 2 is the working tool. For an exchangeable system -- every nucleon the same, so L(S) sees only |S| -- the 2^A - A - 1 subset traces at 3A strands collapse to A - 1 scalar inputs f(k) = L_k, each of which can be computed in its own minimal system of 3k strands because L(S) does not see nucleons outside S. At A = 6 that is five trace pairs, one of them at n = 18, in place of fifty-seven traces at n = 18; it is the difference between an order-six cumulant existing and not.

What is a theorem and what is a measurement

The three items are algebra, true for every set function on every commutative ring, and are proved. The two facts that make the bond model an instance -- that the homonuclear L(S) depends only on |S|, and that it does not see nucleons outside S -- are properties of this particular trace. They are established at 200-bit precision (residuals at the working floor, \sim 10^{-59}, at A = 3, 4, 5), and they are not proved: the Markov-trace properties available are cyclicity and single-generator conjugation, not the split-link tensor rule, and the band routing of a far bond sits between other letters where conjugation invariance does not reach.
